title: Codebase tightness assessment
summary: Zonoid is product-concept tight but implementation-repo tightness is moderate, not high. Strong signals: dependency-free runtime except optional @xenova/transformers, small npm artifact (npm pack dry run: 273 files, 0.87 MB packed / 2.94 MB unpacked), clear daemon/MCP/hook/graph architecture, and 200 test files with ~36.7k test LOC against ~40.7k main JS/TS LOC. Loose signals: repo checkout is dominated by tracked runtime/knowledge state (.graph is intentionally versioned: 2,085 files, ~101 MB, 86 MB nodes, custom merge=ours), checked-in scratch/result artifacts include C:WindowsTemppeek.json 9.3 MB and tmp_graph.json 696 KB, and core behavior is concentrated in large hotspots (daemon.js 2,842 LOC, lib/subconscious/index.js 2,149, packages/cli/bin/zonoid.js 1,569, lib/overlay.js 1,418, routes/overlay.js 1,296). npm test is not green on this snapshot: 197/200 files passed in 215.1s; failures were force-claim-cap.test.js, guidance-resolve.test.js, note-decay-subsumption.test.js. Tightness verdict: strong product thesis and consumer package, but contributor/maintenance tightness is weakened by state-in-repo, large orchestration chokepoints, a bundled 736 KB public/graph.html with duplicated browser logic, stale test docs that still describe npm test as a fast single-gate regression, and current coordination/retrieval regressions.
